answer: Each identity claims one dune segment, stakes 70, and marks both ends with willow stakes bound to its key. It files mean spacing of twenty ripple crests plus its grain sample. An auditor recomputes expected spacing from a public wind-and-grain table; over ten percent off, a reused serial, or overlap burns the bond. First filing 34 credits, kth 34+5(k-1), thousandth 5029; one thousand fakes pay 2,531,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-stake ring fails: one serial cannot serve two keys, and copied spacing mismatches its own grain entry. An honest identity pays 34 once and recovers it if clean.
